# docker_container (Data Source)

Looks up one container on the provider's Docker host by ID or name, like `docker container inspect`. Use it for containers Terraform does not manage; the full inspect response is in `inspect` and `inspect_json`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A container started outside Terraform, for example by a CI agent.
data "docker_container" "agent" {
  name = "ci-agent"
}

output "agent_image" {
  value = data.docker_container.agent.image_id
}

output "agent_running" {
  value = data.docker_container.agent.inspect.state.running
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Container ID (a unique prefix works). Set exactly one of `id` and `name`; the other is filled in.
- `name` (String) Container name, without the leading `/`. Set exactly one of `id` and `name`; the other is filled in.

### Read-Only

- `content_sha256` (String) sha256 of inspect_json.
- `docker_server_version` (String) Docker Engine version from GET /version.
- `engine_api_version` (String) Engine API version negotiated with the daemon (min of the client maximum and GET /version ApiVersion).
- `image_id` (String) ID of the image the container was created from.
- `inspect` (Attributes) The GET /containers/{id}/json response as a nested object, field by field. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--inspect))
- `inspect_json` (String, Sensitive) The exact Engine API GET /containers/{id}/json response as JSON.
- `labels` (Map of String) Container labels (`Config.Labels`).
